This paper introduce RoomGen, a 3D Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) tailored for this purpose. RoomGen integrates an enhanced Variational Autoencoder (VAE) and a UNet++ discriminator for discriminate feature learning. Specifically, VAE introduces residual module in the encoder and deep supervision in the decoder, which improves the fidelity of the generated layouts. In addition, RoomGen incorporates a novel attention mechanism in the UNet++ recognizer, which enables it to capture fine-grained features and better distinguish between real and generated layouts. Experimental results demonstrate RoomGen can proficiently generate high-quality indoor furniture layouts with impressive reconstruction accuracy. Additionally, RoomGen’s capability to produce diverse and realistic scenes offers a more cost-effective solution for the real estate and home improvement sectors. Moreover, it provides a fully automated solution for designing virtual reality scenes and 3D game environments.

articleTitle: A Stealthy Backdoor Attack Method Based on Generative Adversarial Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 Asia-Pacific Conference on Image Processing, Electronics and Computers (IPEC)
abstract: Deep neural networks have been widely and successfully applied to many critical tasks, such as image pattern recognition, natural language processing and autonomous driving, and large amounts of training data and increasing computational power are key factors in their success. Many studies in recent years have shown that deep neural network models face many practical security threats, such as adversarial attacks and backdoor attacks, which can have very serious consequences in the real world. Aiming at the problems of stealth, backdoor trigger design and universality of current backdoor attack methods, a novel method of invisible backdoor attack based on generative adversarial network is proposed. As a backdoor attack method based on data poisoning, inspired by image steganography, this method trains an encoder to generate poisoned samples through generative adversarial network to implement backdoor attack. The secret image used to guide the generation of backdoor triggers does not need to be carefully designed, and the encoder has good generalization ability across datasets. These features not only make its attack effective and stealthy, but also greatly reduce the cost of backdoor. Extensive experimental and analytical results show that the proposed backdoor attack method is effective, stealthy, sustainable and universal.

articleTitle: Robust Image Steganography Model Based on Discrete-Dual-Tree Complex Wavelet Transform and Invertible Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 Asia-Pacific Conference on Image Processing, Electronics and Computers (IPEC)
abstract: Image steganography is a type of method to conceal information within digital images for secure transmission, which has wide applications in the fields of covert transmission and copyright protection. Recently, although image steganography methods based on INNs significantly enhance the hiding capacity, they are exceptionally sensitive to noise and compression during network transmission, and even minor disturbances may have an impact on the recovery of the secret image. Therefore, we come up with a robust image steganography model for INNs based on DDTCWT. This model incorporates a JPEG compression simulation attack module into the network so that the network learns the mapping between the compressed stego and the secret image to resist the JPEG compression attack. Additionally, for the purpose of improving the quality of both the stego and secret images, this method introduces the DTCWT combined with DWT to extract more high-frequency information to help image reconstruction. In order to improve the imperceptibility of the stego image, the model combines transformer with dense block to improve the global modeling capability of INNs. Experimental results demonstrate that our model is robust for JPEG compression compared to existing image steganography methods, while ensuring image quality and capacity.

articleTitle: Design of an English Translation Intelligent Proofreading System Based on Bidirectional Long Short-term Memory Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 Asia-Pacific Conference on Image Processing, Electronics and Computers (IPEC)
abstract: The quality and accuracy of translation play a crucial role in everyday English communication. To enhance translation quality, a specialized smart proofreading system is developed for commonly used English language variations in this paper. Using Amazon Relational Database Service (RDS), the proposed system designs database structures such as statement relationship tables and translation judgment tables. The application interface is programmed in Python, incorporating various view classes like homepage, editing, and display to create the user interface. Leveraging the IaaS cloud platform of Open Nebula and utilizing bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) algorithms, the server-side encoding module is formulated. An information fusion module for word vectors is established, enabling the creation of an intelligent proofreading module through the construction of word and semantic proofreading units. Finally, the simulation study in black-box testing validates the system’s functionalities, the research of this paper shows a substantial improvement in translation quality and notable proofreading advantages.

articleTitle: An Algorithm for Predicting the Running Time of Jobs in Heterogeneous Clusters
publicationTitle: 2024 Asia-Pacific Conference on Image Processing, Electronics and Computers (IPEC)
abstract: With the development of deep learning technology, research on resource scheduling in heterogeneous clusters is increasingly focusing on predicting job running times before resource scheduling, in order to improve the prediction accuracy of heterogeneous cluster job running times. Due to the complexity of system applications in heterogeneous clusters, the success rate of jobs is relatively low, which poses problems for load and stability issues. In order to better improve the prediction accuracy of job running time in heterogeneous clusters, we propose an algorithm that clusters data features, designs a prediction network, and optimizes the network structure. Specifically, we first use K-means algorithm to cluster the data features of job logs in heterogeneous clusters, in order to reduce the discreteness of training data. Secondly, we design a TA-GRU network model for predicting job running time, which can acquire better contextual time information while simplifying the model parameters. Finally, a series of simulation experiments are conducted to verify the algorithm proposed in this paper.

articleTitle: Object Detection for Optical Remote Sensing Images with Self-supervised Feature Representation
publicationTitle: 2024 Asia-Pacific Conference on Image Processing, Electronics and Computers (IPEC)
abstract: Automatically detecting objects of interest on remote sensing images is crucial for earth observations. Existing remote sensing object detectors mainly rely on supervised methods, and the quality and quantity of annotated samples determine the detection performance. However, obtaining large-scale labeled images is labor-intensive and requires domain expertise, which hinders the advancement of remote sensing object detection. To solve the problem, a method based on self-supervised feature representation is presented, with the goal of investigating how to utilize a large number of unlabeled remote-sensing images to enhance detection performance. The method contains three steps. Firstly, the presented method collects many unlabeled remote-sensing photos and reconstructs them to suppress the ineffective expression of background information while preserving the key features of the object. Then, object-level contrastive learning is used to acquire the generalized feature representation. Finally, the extracted feature expression is transferred to downstream task to improve the final detection performance. Experiment results show that with only a few training epochs on the NWPU VHR-10.v2 dataset, the proposed method outperforms supervised-only methods.

articleTitle: Exploration and Optimization of Lottery Ticket Hypothesis for Few-shot Image Classification Task
publicationTitle: 2024 Asia-Pacific Conference on Image Processing, Electronics and Computers (IPEC)
abstract: Few-Shot Learning (FSL) refers to the problem of learning the underlying pattern in the data just from a few training samples. However, when using transfer learning to solve few-shot image classification, deep neural networks have overfitting problems and low training efficiency. Lottery Ticket Hypothesis (LTH), a model pruning method, has gathered great focus since being proposed. This paper explore LTH of few-shot image classification task. Firstly, the search process is proposed to find the winning ticket, and the generalization ability and training efficiency of the model can be improved by training the sparse winning ticket. Secondly, in order to quickly find the winning ticket, an early pruning method was proposed, which included a novel Prune-aware(PA) strategy and Mixed-Precision(MP) training strategy. Experiments on the miniImageNet and $\mathrm{FC100}$ datasets verified the effectiveness of LTH in FSL, and winning tickets can be found faster with PA and MP strategies, which improves the efficiency of the search process. Early pruning method achieves a balance between accuracy and efficiency while mitigating the overfitting problem in few-shot learning.

articleTitle: Research of Russian Conversion Algorithm based on Hidden Markov Model
publicationTitle: 2024 Asia-Pacific Conference on Image Processing, Electronics and Computers (IPEC)
abstract: Phonetic conversion technology is pivotal in developing resources for Russian speech information processing. This paper aims to enhance the Russian phoneme set based on SAMPA, ensuring accurate reflection of stress position and vowel reduction in Russian words. Utilizing the improved phoneme set, this paper successfully constructed a Russian pronunciation dictionary with 20,000 words. A data-driven Russian phonetic conversion algorithm leveraging the Hidden Markov Model (HMM) for alignment, modeling, and decoding is proposed. Initially, the Expectation-Maximization algorithm aligns Russian phonetics in a “many-to-many” manner. Subsequently, alignment results are trained using a joint N-gram model and transformed into a HMM pronunciation model. The HMM decoding algorithm ultimately predicts word pronunciation accurately. Cross-validation experiments yielded satisfactory results, and they show that the proposed can be easily implemented in the computer assisted system and provide enhanced accuracy and convenience to the Russian conversion process.
